newsitem.title: THAILAND: Shan rebels say Burmese troops massacre civilians.
newsitem.headline: Shan rebels say Burmese troops massacre civilians.

text.p: The ethnic Shan resistance faction on Tuesday accused Burmese troops of massacring 58 civilians in Shan state last month, Shan and Thai army sources said.

The Shan State Army (SSA) said in a statement obtained by Reuters that on June 6, Burmese troops arrested 26 people in Chianglom village of Kunhing district. The troops said the people had relocated without permission.
The statement said all 26 villagers were tied up and shot dead at close range.

"The Burmese soldiers have seriously violated human rights in Shan State," it said. "The Burmese army ... tied up 26 people and killed them in cold blood at close range. The people were only accused of violating an order not to relocate."
Similar incidents occurred on June 10 and 16 when 32 people were killed in two villages of Kunhing district, the statement added.
Burmese government officials were not immediately available for comment.
A Thai army source based on the border said he had heard about the incident from Shan refugees who fled to Thailand, but added he had not been able to confirm the number of victims.

A veteran Shan guerrilla told Reuters from the border that the massacres occurred after Burma's military government, known as the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) began its "four-cut" operation against the rebels, who are fighting for autonomy for central Shan state.
"The four-cut operation began since May as the SLORC is trying to cut the people from the resistance groups," the guerrilla said.
The operation is intended to deprive the rebels of information, supplies and other assistance, and to block their recruiting and propaganda efforts, he said.
The Burmese government said last month that the former Mong Tai Army (MTA) guerrillas of opium warlord Khun Sa had killed 25 civilians in eastern Shan state in early June.
The SSA is a loose grouping of fighters who broke away from the MTA before Khun Sa surrendered to the Burmese troops in January 1996.

Khun Sa was the half-Shan, half-Chinese commander of the MTA who said he was fighting for independence of Shan state. But international drugs agencies accused him of using the MTA as his personal army to protect his heroin business.
Khun Sa denied the accusations. He is said to be living a life of luxury in Rangoon since his surrender.
